name: PCI-DSS v4.0.1
description: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard v4.0.1. 12 requirements organized into 6 control objectives. This audit covers the subset applicable to any website, plus payment-specific checks prepared for planned payment integration.
honest_disclosure: This site does not currently process, store, or transmit cardholder data (CHD). PCI-DSS is not in scope. The universal web security checks below are best practice. Items marked 'not_applicable' will become assessable when payment pages are deployed. When payment integration begins, the site will fall under SAQ A (simplest scope — fully outsourced payments).
future_scoping_note: When payments are integrated via a validated TPSP (Stripe, PayPal, Braintree), this site will be eligible for SAQ A. SAQ A covers requirements 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 — but NOT requirements 1, 3, 4, 10 (which are covered by the TPSP's compliance).

assessability_legend.universal: Applies to any website, regardless of payment processing
assessability_legend.http_live: Verifiable via live HTTP response headers
assessability_legend.not_applicable: Not applicable — no CDE or payment processing
assessability_legend.payment_required: Will apply when payment pages are deployed (future)

group_policies.name: Req 2: Apply Secure Configurations to All System Components
group_policies.description: NIST SP 800-53 CM-6 — configuration standards, least functionality, vendor defaults

items.description: Req 2.2.4: Implement additional security features for required services/protocols deemed insecure. No sensitive files exposed (.git, .env, backups).
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 2.2.4 — secure system configurations
items.remediation: Remove all sensitive configuration and backup files from web-accessible directories.

items.description: Req 2.2.1: Configuration standards address known security vulnerabilities and industry best practices (CIS Benchmarks, DISA STIGs).
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 2.2.1 — configuration standards
items.remediation: Document and implement configuration standards aligned with CIS Benchmarks for all system components.

group_policies.name: Req 4: Protect Cardholder Data with Strong Cryptography During Transmission
group_policies.description: NIST SC-8 — TLS 1.2+ for all CHD transmission. If no CHD is transmitted, this is a universal best practice.

items.description: Req 4.2.1: Strong cryptography and security protocols (TLS 1.2+) must be used for all transmission of cardholder data over open, public networks. Universal web security best practice regardless of CHD scope.
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 4.2.1 — secure transmission; NIST SC-8
items.remediation: Deploy TLS 1.2+ with valid certificate. All pages that handle or precede payment must be served over HTTPS.

items.description: Req 4.2.1.1: Maintain an inventory of trusted keys and certificates. Track expiry dates, certificate authorities, and key strengths.
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 4.2.1.1 — certificate inventory
items.remediation: Create and maintain a documented inventory of all TLS certificates with expiry dates and CA information.

group_policies.name: Req 6: Develop and Maintain Secure Systems and Software
group_policies.description: NIST SI-2 — patch management, secure development, web application protection, payment page script integrity

items.description: Req 6.2.4: All software components must be maintained and patched. No known-vulnerable CDN library versions (jQuery 1.x/2.x, Bootstrap <4, Font Awesome <5).
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 6.2.4 — software maintenance; NIST SI-2
items.remediation: Update all CDN libraries to current versions. Remove deprecated jQuery and Bootstrap versions.

items.description: Req 6.4.2: Deploy an automated technical solution (WAF or similar) that continually detects and prevents web-based attacks on public-facing web applications. Must protect against OWASP Top 10 and generate audit logs/alerts.
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 6.4.2 — web application firewall; NIST SC-7
items.remediation: Deploy a WAF (Cloudflare, AWS WAF, ModSecurity) in front of the web server. Configure to block OWASP Top 10 attacks and log all blocked requests.

group_policies.name: Req 7 & 8: Access Control & Authentication
group_policies.description: NIST AC-6, IA-2 — least privilege, unique IDs, MFA for CDE access

items.description: Req 7.2.2: Access to system components and data is assigned to individuals based on job classification and function (least privilege).
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 7.2.2 — access control; NIST AC-6
items.remediation: Document access roles. Restrict server/site deployment access to authorized personnel only.

items.description: Req 8.3.1: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is implemented for all access into the CDE (Cardholder Data Environment).
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 8.3.1 — MFA for CDE; NIST IA-2(1)
items.remediation: Implement MFA for all administrative access to systems in the CDE. Use TOTP, FIDO2, or certificate-based MFA.

items.description: Req 8.3.9: If passwords are the only authentication factor, they must be changed at least every 90 days or a security posture assessment must justify alternative frequency.
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 8.3.9 — password rotation
items.remediation: Configure password rotation policy: 90-day maximum, or implement MFA as primary factor.

group_policies.name: Req 11: Test Security of Systems and Networks Regularly
group_policies.description: NIST RA-5 — vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, file integrity monitoring, payment page tamper detection

items.description: Req 11.3.1.2: External vulnerability scans must be performed by a PCI ASV (Approved Scanning Vendor) at least quarterly. Required for SAQ A merchants with redirect/iframe.
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 11.3.1.2 — ASV scans; NIST RA-5
items.remediation: Schedule quarterly external vulnerability scans with a PCI ASV. Rescan until passing grade achieved.

items.description: Req 11.6.1 [FUTURE-DATED — effective 31 Mar 2025]: Deploy change- and tamper-detection mechanism to alert on unauthorized modification to security headers and script contents of payment pages (client-side). Works with Req 6.4.3 for e-commerce skimming protection.
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 11.6.1 — payment page tamper detection
items.remediation: When payment pages are deployed: implement CSP reporting, SRI integrity monitoring, and client-side script change detection.

items.description: Req 11.5.2: Deploy file integrity monitoring (FIM) or change-detection mechanism on critical system files. Alert on unauthorized modifications.
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 11.5.2 — file integrity monitoring; NIST SI-7
items.remediation: Deploy FIM (AIDE, Tripwire, OSSEC) on critical system files. Configure alerts for unauthorized changes.

group_policies.name: Req 3 & 5: Data Protection & Malware
group_policies.description: Requirements that apply when CHD is stored or when systems are in CDE scope

items.description: Req 3.4.1: PAN must be masked when displayed (maximum first six and last four digits visible). No unmasked credit card numbers or SSNs in HTML source, localStorage, or JavaScript.
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 3.4.1 — PAN masking
items.remediation: Never include unmasked PAN (credit card numbers) in HTML source code, JavaScript, or localStorage.

items.description: Req 5.2.1: Anti-malware solution(s) must be deployed on all systems commonly affected by malicious software. Required for SAQ A merchant systems.
items.remediation: Deploy anti-malware on all merchant systems. Ensure real-time scanning and automatic updates.

group_policies.name: Req 12: Information Security Policy
group_policies.description: Organizational policies, security awareness, incident response, TPSP management

items.description: Req 12.5.1: PCI DSS scope must be documented and validated at least annually. Define all system components in scope, including connected-to and security-impacting systems.
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 12.5.1 — scope documentation
items.remediation: Document PCI DSS scope, including network diagrams, data flow diagrams, and system inventory. Review and update annually.

items.description: Req 12.10.1: An incident response plan must be documented, maintained, and tested at least annually. Must include roles, responsibilities, communication procedures, and business recovery processes.
items.regulation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 12.10.1 — incident response
items.remediation: Create and maintain an incident response plan. Test annually with tabletop exercises or actual incident simulations.
